  Move ALL DSML parsing/judgment/documentation out of internal/toolcall:

  - internal/toolcall/dsml_doc.go -> internal/dsml/doc.go (package dsml)

  The execution kernel stays in internal/toolcall: ToolDef, ToolArgs, ToolContent, the registry (RegisterTool/GetToolDef/KnownToolNames), and the tool executor. To let dsml use them, EXPORT these four from internal/toolcall (rename the unexported ones and update all internal callers):

  1. `func RoleToolsSpec(ctx context.Context, role string) string` (was roleToolsSpec)
  2. `func RoleToolAllowSet(ctx context.Context, role string) map[string]bool` (was roleToolAllowSet)
  3. `func AllowSetFromSpec(spec string) map[string]bool` (was allowSetFromSpec)
  4. `func ExecuteToolCalls(ctx context.Context, tcs []prompt.ToolCall, save bool) (outcomes []ToolCallOutcome, dualUsers []prompt.Message)` (was executeToolCalls; update HandleToolCalls to call it)

Implement it in internal/toolcall/tool.go using the same logic as the existing test helper unregisterToolForTest (lock, delete from toolRegistry and toolAliases).

Keep the internal/context import for the role fallback in the allow-set helper (CurrentRoleKey, "dev"). No other package references dsml (no import cycle: dsml -> toolcall only).

  ## 2. Exported API (internal/dsml)

  Keep these exported names working exactly as before (just package-renamed): HasDSMLToolCalls, IsPureDSMLToolCalls, IsDSMLToolCallEnd, IsDSMLToolCallCut, IsDSMLToolCallReply, ParseDSMLToolCalls(text string) ([]DSMLCall, error), StripDSMLToolCalls, ExecuteDSMLToolCalls(ctx, calls []DSMLCall) []string, BuildDSMLToolDoc(ctx, role) prompt.DSMLToolDoc.

  Add:

  ```go
  // SuspectedDSMLToolCalls reports text that clearly attempts a tool call but parses to zero calls or errors:
  // HasDSMLToolCalls(text) is true AND (ParseDSMLToolCalls(text) fails OR returns 0 calls).
  func SuspectedDSMLToolCalls(text string) bool

  const StrictWarning = "WARNING: your tool-call markup did not strictly follow the required format (e.g. extra attribute such as justification, missing string=\"true|false\" attribute, unclosed or stray tags); the call was accepted but you MUST strictly follow the exact format in the tool schema for every future call."

  const ReissueWarning = "WARNING: your reply appears to contain a DSML tool call but it could not be parsed. Please re-send the tool call(s) strictly following the required format: <tool_calls><invoke name=\"...\"><parameter name=\"...\" string=\"true|false\">...</parameter></invoke></tool_calls>. Do not include extra attributes such as justification."

  // InjectStrictWarning injects StrictWarning into the warning field of each <tool_result>{...}</tool_result> block in outputs.
  // If a block already has a warning, append (newline-separated). Skip blocks whose JSON has no result/error/warning.
  // Parse the inner JSON into a map[string]any, set "warning" (append), re-marshal, re-wrap <tool_result>...</tool_result>.
  func InjectStrictWarning(outputs []string) []string

  // ParseDSMLMessage parses one webchat assistant reply into a protocol Message.
  func ParseDSMLMessage(reasoning string, content string) prompt.Message
  ```

  ## 3. ParseDSMLMessage semantics

  Source rule: content first. If parsing content yields calls, use content as source and leave reasoning untouched (original). If content yields zero calls AND reasoning non-empty AND HasDSMLToolCalls(reasoning), parse reasoning and use it as source.

  Add an internal strict-parser: `parseDSMLToolCallsStrict(text string) (calls []DSMLCall, err error, violated bool)`. Refactor ParseDSMLToolCalls to call it and discard violated (keep its public signature and existing behavior).

  Violation flags (set violated=true at each tolerance point; a bool is enough):

  1. normalizeDSMLText(text) != text (fullwidth->halfwidth, entity junk, zero-width chars, tag junk were repaired).
  2. The parse loop sees a parameter named "justification" (currently kept in Args; still keep it in Args for backward-compat of ParseDSMLToolCalls, but flag violation).
  3. dsmlBlockRanges reports strays (extra </invoke>). Modify dsmlBlockRanges to also return `implicit int` (count of implicit closes in the wrapper-close-at-end branch); flag violation if implicit > 0.
  4. A parameter missing the string="true|false" attribute (dsmlParamRe group 2 empty).
  5. A nested invoke block got masked inside another block body (the nested-masking loop in ParseDSMLToolCalls).
  6. Wrapper close at end is a typo or cut: on the trimmed NORMALIZED text, if it ends with a wrapper close that is NOT exactly </tool_calls> (i.e. </_calls>, <_calls>, or a cut-off </... as matched by dsmlToolCallsCloseCutRe), flag violation.
  7. Bare invoke: calls parsed but there is NO wrapper close tag at end at all (IsPureDSMLToolCalls path with no wrapper) - flag violation.

  Repeated <parameter> for the same name (array semantics) is NOT a violation.

  ParseDSMLMessage output:
  - Convert parsed calls via the existing dsmlCallsToToolCalls to []prompt.ToolCall (msg.ToolCalls = tcs).
  - msg.Role = "assistant". msg.Content and msg.ReasoningContent default to the raw inputs.
  - OK = (len(ToolCalls) > 0) && !violated.
  - If len(ToolCalls) > 0 and !violated: strip the SOURCE (StripDSMLToolCalls of content if source==content, else StripDSMLToolCalls of reasoning into ReasoningContent; the other field stays original).
  - If violated: keep source original (do NOT strip) - caller can fall back.
  - If zero calls: ToolCalls nil, Content/ReasoningContent original, OK=false.
  - If parse err (truncated): zero calls, OK=false.

  ## 4. Strict prompt wording in BuildDSMLToolDoc (internal/dsml/doc.go)

  In the Intro, after the "You have access to a set of tools..." paragraph and before the example loop, add an English paragraph covering: every call must be a complete <tool_calls> block wrapping <invoke name="...">; every parameter must be <parameter name="..." string="true|false">; NO extra attributes (such as justification) and NO parameters beyond the example; all tags must be closed (</invoke>, </tool_calls>); one reply may contain multiple <invoke> elements (independent calls), dependent calls must wait for previous results; output must be structurally identical to the example (the example is the authoritative format). Keep the trailing Schemas sentence "You MUST strictly follow the above defined tool name and parameter schemas to invoke tool calls."

  ## 5. Rework internal/lp/handle.go handleWebChatToolLoop (about lines 513-580)

  Change `var handleWebChatExecDSML = toolcall.ExecuteDSMLToolCalls` to `= dsml.ExecuteDSMLToolCalls` (import internal/dsml; keep internal/toolcall import if still used elsewhere in the file).

  Track lastReasoning: before the loop set `lastReasoning := first.Reasoning`; at the end of each iteration after printRound(res) set `lastReasoning = res.Reasoning`.

  New loop body per round:

  ```
  msg := dsml.ParseDSMLMessage(lastReasoning, message)
  switch {
  case len(msg.ToolCalls) > 0 && dsml.IsDSMLToolCallReply(message):
      calls, _ := dsml.ParseDSMLToolCalls(message)
      fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "🤖 %s 请求执行 %d 个工具调用（第 %d/%d 轮）…\n", roleName, len(calls), round, handleWebChatMaxDSMLRounds)
      outputs := handleWebChatExecDSML(ctx, calls)
      if len(outputs) == 0 {
          fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "⚠️ %s 回复只包含非可执行工具调用（未在角色工具配置中或引用示例？），已跳过执行\n", roleName)
          return cleanExit()
      }
      feedback := buildWebChatFeedback(outputs)
      if !msg.OK {
          fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "⚠️ 工具调用格式不够严格，已执行并告警\n")
          feedback = dsml.InjectStrictWarning(feedback)
      }
      followUp := WebChatOptions{Mode: opts.Mode, Keep: convURL}
      res, callErr := handleWebChatSend(ctx, feedback, followUp)
      if callErr != nil { return WebChatResult{}, fmt.Errorf("webchat tool loop: continue conversation during round %d: %w", round, callErr) }
      message = res.Content
      if res.URL != "" { convURL = res.URL }
      printRound(res)
      lastReasoning = res.Reasoning
  case len(msg.ToolCalls) > 0 && !dsml.IsDSMLToolCallReply(message):
      return cleanExit()
  case len(msg.ToolCalls) == 0 && dsml.SuspectedDSMLToolCalls(message):
      fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "⚠️ 工具调用疑似但解析失败，已要求重发\n")
      followUp := WebChatOptions{Mode: opts.Mode, Keep: convURL}
      res, callErr := handleWebChatSend(ctx, dsml.ReissueWarning, followUp)
      if callErr != nil { return WebChatResult{}, fmt.Errorf("webchat tool loop: reissue warning during round %d: %w", round, callErr) }
      message = res.Content
      if res.URL != "" { convURL = res.URL }
      printRound(res)
      lastReasoning = res.Reasoning
  default:
      return cleanExit()
  }
  ```

  Keep the existing cleanExit and printRound closures and the trailing over-limit warning exactly as they are, EXCEPT cleanExit's strip call becomes dsml.StripDSMLToolCalls. Keep the existing "⚠️ 远程模型回复中的 DSML 工具调用..." stderr line and the round-cap exit.
